chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Sufi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Hamza ibn al-Qasim narrated to us. He said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Wazzan narrated to us from Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ahwazi. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Humran. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said:

When you enter the bathhouse, say at the moment you remove your clothes: "O Allah, remove from me the yoke of hypocrisy and make me steadfast upon faith." When you enter the first chamber, say: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of my self, and I seek refuge in You from its harm." When you enter the second chamber, say: "O Allah, remove from me the filthy impurity and purify my body and my heart." Then take hot water and place it on your head, and pour some on your legs. If you can swallow a sip of it, do so, for it purifies the bladder. Stay in the second chamber for a while. When you enter the third chamber, say: "We seek refuge in Allah from the Fire, and we ask Him for Paradise" -- repeat it until you leave the hot chamber. Beware of drinking cold water and fuqqa' in the bathhouse, for it upsets the stomach. Do not pour cold water on yourself, for it weakens the body. But pour cold water on your feet when you leave, for it draws disease out of your body. When you put on your clothes, say: "O Allah, dress me in God-consciousness and spare me from destruction." If you do this, you will be safe from every ailment.

key_terms.التقوى: Taqwa - God-consciousness, piety, awareness of the divine
key_terms.الحمام: Hammam - the traditional public bathhouse with multiple heated chambers
key_terms.الرجس النجس: The filthy impurity - both physical and spiritual uncleanliness
key_terms.الفقاع: Fuqqa' - a fermented barley drink common in medieval Islamic lands
key_terms.ربقة النفاق: The yoke/bond of hypocrisy - metaphor for the constraining effect of insincerity

ai.seo_question: What are the Islamic supplications and etiquette for entering a bathhouse according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides comprehensive instructions for visiting the public bathhouse (hammam), combining specific supplications with practical health advice. The teaching was given in the context of the traditional multi-chambered public baths of the early Islamic period, where each room had a different temperature. The Imam integrates spiritual purification (removing hypocrisy, seeking refuge from the self's evil) with physical hygiene advice (hot water for the head, cold water only for the feet), reflecting Islam's holistic approach to bodily and spiritual well-being.

en.bilal-muhammad: Al-Husayn b. `Ali al-Sufi (ra) narrated to us. He said: Hamza b. al-Qasim narrated to us. He said: Ja`far b. Muhammad b. Malik narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Wazzan narrated to us from Yahya b. Sa`id al-Ahwazi. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Abi Nasr narrated to us from Muhammad b. Hamza. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as) said:

When you enter the restroom, then say when you remove your clothing: “O Allah! Remove hypocrisy from me and make me steadfast upon faith (Allahummanzi` `anni ribqatul nifaq wa tathbitni `alal iman).” When you enter the first chamber, then say: “O Allah! I seek refuge in You from the evil of my self, and I seek refuge in you from its harm (Allahumma inni `a’udhu bika min sharri nafsi wasta`eedh bika min adhah).” When you enter the second chamber, then say: “O Allah! Cleanse me of impurity and purify my body and my heart (Allahummadhhab `annil rijsil najis, wa tahhir jasadi wa qalbi)”, then take hot water and put it on your hips and pour it on your legs. If you can swallow some, then do so, for that purifies the bladder. Then, wait in the second chamber for a moment. When you enter the third chamber, then say: “We seek refuge in Allah from the Fire, and we ask Him for Paradise (na`udhu billahi min an-nar, wa nas’aluhul Jannah)”. Repeat it until the moment you exit the hot chamber. Beware of drinking cold water and bubbles in the restroom, for it upsets the digestive system. Do not pour cold water over yourself, for it weakens the body. Pour cold water on your feet when you leave, for that will remove disease from your body. When you get dressed, then say: “O Allah! Dress me in God-consciousness and spare me of harm (Allahummalbisnil taqwa wa jannibnil rida)” – if you do this, you will be safe from every disease.
